channel.title: The Talas Herald
channel.description: News from Talas and across Irad.

item.title: Toktogul's extra 240 MW raises the question of who shares the revenue
item.description: All four units now run at 360 MW, but the cost of the refit and the formula that divides export income remain unpublished.

item.title: Antimony restart relies on partners the combine has not named
item.description: About IS 125 million is to reopen idled lines at Sary-Bulak and Chatkal; a mercury unit at the smelter will need a new permit and a public hearing.

item.title: Tashkent calls water scarcity a brake on the region as Naryn talks near
item.description: Uzbekistan's president urged digital monitoring and canal repairs at a summit in Turkmenistan; Irad's negotiators say the 2027 Naryn schedule will need the same data.

item.title: Rabat-i-Safed coins to be tested in Nurzhan as museum asks for custody
item.description: The heritage permit for the dig says finds go to the national museum; the university wants to keep the Kara-Khanid coins until its study is published.

item.title: Thirty new schools deserve one published budget
item.description: The building programme is welcome. Its total cost and its timetable should be public.

item.title: Supreme Court puts its case register online; inability petition awaits a date
item.description: The new public docket lists 214 pending matters, among them the June petition on the Elective Governor Acts, marked as awaiting listing.

item.title: Komuz contest is open to highland players, if they can get travel permits
item.description: The rules for the Aigul Choro kyzy competition welcome entrants from across the line, but clan permits must be registered with the Gendarmerie before 22 October.

item.title: Boztorgoy and Karakoyun stay perfect as ulak league reaches round four
item.description: In Talas a Chicago-born fighter rode with the city team in training, but Directorate rules keep unlicensed guests out of league play.

item.title: Navbahor school cost IS 31.5 million, council papers show
item.description: The solar-roofed school opened by the Lieutenant Governor on Monday is one of 30 due this year, but the programme's total budget has not been published.

item.title: Prosecutors ask court to wind up 16 trade-zone firms over sanctions risk
item.description: The applications follow a review of about 40 companies by the Foreign Trade Escrow Authority, and Talasbank has closed the accounts of some 120 firms.

item.title: Ministry proposes halting potato imports until March as harvest outruns demand
item.description: Growers in the Talas valley welcome the draft, but the self-sufficiency rate it cites does not match the ministry's own forecasts.

item.title: Swiss wind orchestra to march down Liberty Boulevard on 18 October
item.description: The 100-strong band from Fribourg will also play with the Talas Symphony Orchestra at the Philharmonic Hall, and the city has approved a four-hour road closure.

item.title: Nurzhan's new boiler houses should come with a published gas price
item.description: The council has paid for the plants. It should now show residents what the heat will cost.

item.title: Court adjourns stallholders' claim over Jibek Jolu market fire
item.description: Thirty-eight traders seeking IS 3.1 million from the market's operator and the city must wait for the fire service's report, a Talas District Court judge ruled.

item.title: Nurzhan council approves IS 10.4 million for two local boiler houses
item.description: The gas-fired plants are meant to take about 6,900 homes on the city's outer estates off the central network before the heating season begins.

item.title: Russian cap on cash rubles hits families who carry savings home
item.description: A new limit of 1 million rubles a person at crossings into Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan will push more migrants' earnings through transfer services and Talasbank.

item.title: FFI fines Naryn Tash-Kömür IS 25,000 over unequipped medical room
item.description: The bottom club was punished in the week Tulpar Talas beat it 7–0 to go six points clear with four rounds left.

item.title: Lieutenant Governor's office sets IS 41 million for school textbooks
item.description: Every new book will carry a code tracing it to a school and a pupil, after free Iradi-language readers turned up for sale near the Bazar-i Kalan.
